title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-12-01
source: SBD -> Reel Master -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD -> EAC -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Top‑notch soundboard capture of a high‑energy Boston set featuring a smoking “Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One” sequence and stellar playing from Jerry, Phil and the new keyboards.
ai_review.review: The second set from the December 1, 1971 Boston Music Hall show is praised for its crystal‑clear SBD source and an electrifying performance that highlights the Cryptical Envelopment intro into a monster “The Other One,” plus a tight Me & My Uncle. Reviewers rave about Jerry’s zone‑filled guitar, Phil’s bass ninja work, Keith’s solid early keyboards and Mickey’s driving drums, making this a must‑listen for any 1971 Dead collection.

ai_rating.rationale: All 13 reviews are 5‑star and uniformly praise both the musical performance (standout songs, high energy) and the excellent soundboard recording; thus the combined rating is near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Consistently described as crisp, great‑sounding SBD with no noted dropouts or balance issues; listeners note it sounds “top notch” and ideal for archival listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second‑set flow centers on the classic TOT → MAMU → TOT sequence, delivering a seamless, high‑octane journey that fans describe as a “collision course Dark Star” vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as "in the zone" with perfect guitar tone and a powerful opening riff of Weather Report Suite woven into The Other One.
band_member_comments.Phil: "Bass ninja"; flexes his muscles during The Other One, delivering strong, melodic bass lines.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux is noted as early‑stage but adds plenty without detracting; his contributions are praised for pointing the way forward.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s presence is highlighted as essential, with drums described as solid and driving.
